column1: # THE STRUCTURAL SUB-SLICES DISCOVERED IN THE LIVE SOURCE.
# Each row is a DECISION INSIDE an enclosing C function, bound to an
# exact source range, classified against the ACT section 7.1 candidate
# requirements and the ACT section 7.2 significance list.

column7: Switch-arm termination decision: given the parsed statement's AstKind, decide whether the case arm's statement loop terminates
column8: AstKind enum value of the parsed statement (one bounded int, copied out of the host Ast node)

column7: Default-arm termination decision: given the parsed statement's AstKind, decide whether the default arm's statement loop terminates
column8: AstKind enum value of the parsed statement (one bounded int, copied out of the host Ast node)

column7: Compound-block statement routing decision: given a parsed statement, decide whether it is appended to the block's statement list or skipped because it is a global-variable declaration
column8: AstKind of the statement AND AstKind of its declvar (two bounded ints copied out of the host Ast node)
column9: one bounded boolean "append to the block statement list"

column7: Statement keyword dispatch decision: given a keyword token value, decide which statement constructor the parser must route to
Declaration-versus-statement routing decision: given the peeked token, decide whether the parser must route to the declaration parser or the statement parser
column8: the peeked token BYTES (an unbounded host buffer) consulted against the MUTABLE host symbol table, class-def map and union-def map
column15: The decision is not a pure token classification: cctrlIsKeyword consults the MUTABLE host symbol table (cc->symbol_table), the class-def map and the union-def map. The decision therefore depends on host symbol-table state, so the projection is not bounded.

column7: Per-statement recovery checkpoint and AST-list tail rollback: decide, after a longjmp, which statements survive in the recovered block
column8: jmp_buf identity, the body->stms tail pointer and the cc->tmp_locals tail pointer
column9: none (the decision is the recovery protocol itself)
column14: Owns the setjmp recovery point and the host linked-list tail rollback; the decision IS the host recovery protocol and has no bounded scalar projection

column7: The whole compound-statement body loop: parse declarations and statements into the block scope and the block statement list
column8: the whole host parser state (token stream, scope, AST list, recovery point)
column14: Whole-function ABI is unbounded: it owns the recovery point, the scope map, the AST list and 30 subordinate calls

column7: The whole statement parser: dispatch on the token and construct the host AST node
column14: Whole-function ABI is unbounded: it owns the scope, the global AST list and the asm-block list

column7: The whole expression loop: build the operator precedence tree
column14: Whole-function ABI is unbounded: it builds the host AST and owns the precedence loop

column7: Control-flow fall-through classification of a statement
column9: one bounded boolean per node, but only through recursion
column14: Recursive walk over an unbounded host statement tree; the projection is not bounded

column7: Control-flow break classification of a statement
column9: one bounded boolean per node, but only through recursion
column14: Recursive walk over an unbounded host statement tree; the projection is not bounded

column8: the host Ast node and its AstType
column14: Three-hop host Ast/AstType pointer chain; the projection is one scalar but the input is an unbounded host pointer
